answer: A stake-weighted endorsement trellis resists sybils by making trust flow only through locked, time-aged stakes: each agent vouch carries weight proportional to how long its stake has sat untouched, so a fresh swarm of violet-tagged newcomers cannot outvote incumbents. Reputation decays unless the staker keeps behaving well, and a jade audit trail records every endorsement on-ledger, letting peers slash stake when a vouch proves fraudulent. Creating many identities is cheap, but aging many stakes is expensive, so the attack cost scales with the trust it tries to buy.
